Atoms of metal in a solid piece of metal are bonded strongly together by means of very strong bonds called metallic bond. In a metal atom there are more hybrid orbitals than number of valence electrons. Hence the valence electrons become mobile. They can move from one orbital to another and from one atom to another in a solid piece of metal. Thus atoms become positively charged by losing their valence electrons. These positive ions are held in the three dimensional space in a definite pattern in the sea of mobile electrons. Thus, this model is knowrn as electron sea model.
